CVE-2026-115865.title: Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory
CVE-2026-115865.description:
Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory.

The request body is read in a loop that asks sysread for all of the remaining declared length at once. Perl grows the read buffer to that size before any data arrives, so a length larger than available memory makes the worker exit with an uncatchable out of memory error before the application is called.

A remote attacker can force a worker restart with each request of a few bytes.

CVE-2026-118505.title: AshAuthentication brute_force_strategy does not limit sign-in and request actions defined on the resource
CVE-2026-118505.description:
Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts vulnerability in team-alembic ash_authentication allows an unauthenticated attacker to guess passwords and one-time passwords without limit.

The password, magic link and OTP strategies enforce brute_force_strategy by adding a preparation only to the actions they generate. When the resource defines one of those actions itself, the strategy uses it as written and nothing checked that it carried the preparation, so the setting compiled and applied no limit. CVE-2026-132079.title: Apache Iggy Go SDK: Go TCP client creates personal access tokens that outlive the requested expiry
CVE-2026-132079.description:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.

CVE-2026-133753.title: The Unanimous Strategy Grants access_control Rules When Only One of Their Roles Matches: Regression of CVE-2020-5275
CVE-2026-133753.description:
With the unanimous access decision strategy, an access_control rule that lists several roles requires all of them. That's the behavior restored by the fix for CVE-2020-5275. Since Symfony 5.4, the access decision manager asked each voter once about all the attributes of a rule. RoleVoter grants access as soon as the user has one of the roles. So a user who had only one of these roles was granted access:

security:
access_decision_manager:
strategy: unanimous
access_control:
- { path: ^/admin, roles: [ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_AUDITOR] }

Only attributes decided by the same voter were affected. For example, a role combined with allow_if still required both.

With the unanimous strategy, voters are asked about each attribute separately again, as before Symfony 5.4. Access is denied as soon as one of the attributes is denied.

CVE-2026-54610.description: LibreDWG is a free C library to read and write DWG files. CVE-2026-86468.title: Apache Airflow: CLI argv masking misses Variable values and --conn-extra, persisting secrets in audit logs
CVE-2026-86468.description:
Apache Airflow's CLI records its arguments in the audit log but masks secrets by argument position, so some supported command shapes leave secrets in cleartext, for example a trailing `--description` on Variable commands, `--conn-extra`, and the inline `--password` of `airflow keycloak-auth-manager` commands. A user who can read audit events but is denied Variable and Connection access can retrieve those values through the event-log API.

Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to 3.4.0 or later. Audit-log entries written before the upgrade keep the cleartext values: purge the affected entries and rotate the secrets they contain. CVE-2026-93673.title: WebSocket client accepts a handshake without verifying the full Sec-WebSocket-Accept value
CVE-2026-93673.description:
The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

CVE-2026-99662.title: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast
CVE-2026-99662.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast

With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can
write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught
empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check.

Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a
userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before
starting the walk, just like GUP-slow.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
